claims.text: The initially solid Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles are in a disordered solid-solution state.
Local chemical heterogeneities in Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles create regions of reduced cohesive energy.
Regions of reduced cohesive energy act as nucleation sites for surface disordering.
Nucleation of surface disordering causes premelting below the bulk melting point.
Differences in constituent atomic radii and bonding strengths produce local compositional fluctuations and diverse surface atomic configurations.
Atomic-scale chemical inhomogeneity in the HEA produces domains with locally reduced cohesive energy.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles will begin surface disordering at lower temperatures than similarly sized single-metal or chemically uniform binary nanoparticles.
Premelting will manifest as reduced crystallinity or altered diffraction patterns.
Surface disordering will preferentially begin at locations with notable compositional variation.
Single-metal or chemically uniform binary baseline nanoparticles exhibit more homogeneous melting without an early onset of surface premelting.
For particles below approximately 100 nm, surface effects and local compositional variations dominate the melting response.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger particles or to HEAs with markedly different compositional distributions.
Current measurement resolution limits prevent precise determination of the temperature shift and spatial correlation between chemical heterogeneity and disorder onset.
